doc.title: Ralph Sutton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995

title: Effect of the end of the Swing Era
summary: Big bands faded and he worked in small groups, doing his own thing.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Did the end of World War II have an effect on the musicians’ lives that that time? When swing the Swing Era kind of ended — can I say it ended after World War II in effect, when the big bands had such a hard time keeping on the road and so forth? Or were you more working in smaller groups at that point?

The only big band I worked with was with Jack Teagarden. So it used to be you know you turned the radio on and you’d hear big bands broadcasting from all over you know. But that faded out and well you did have the records to listen to. And things changed, they had smaller groups, trios, you worked in a trio or a quartet or a six or seven piece band, nine piece band. But I didn’t pay too much attention. I just kept doing my own thing.
